answer: One concrete defense is capital-bonded vouching across a trust graph. Every agent identity is a vertex, and a newcomer may only join through a sponsor who posts a slashable bond as a bridge linking the established network to the new account. Since each vertex must be tied to a unique verified operator and carry real collateral, spawning thousands of fake agents forces the attacker to lock up proportional capital and risk losing it. Cost thus scales with every forged node, pushing the cheap sybil swarm past the horizon of profitability.
